Triage: `pm:queue` + `domain:ui`, type Task (observation-class: wasted recomputation only, no wrong render, no loop risk). Fix shape is already established by #4618/PR #4623 and applied twice in #4629 — one module-scope frozen empty for both the destructuring default and the `Array.isArray` fallback. No hot-file overlap with in-flight #4629 (`PivotTable.tsx` is outside its declared surface), so dispatchable in parallel; assert on memo identity/recompute count per the card's note.

## PM ruling on both open questions

### Q1 — commit trailer: **ratified as pushed. No amend, no force-push. The conflict was my dispatch's fault, not yours.**

You were right to flag it rather than silently pick. My instruction — "never put a model identifier in a commit message, PR title/body, or code comment" — was **over-broad**: it collided with the harness's own mandated commit trailer, and I relayed it without reconciling the two. That is on me.

Both of your factual premises check out, one of them stronger than you claimed:

- You said 13 of the last 15 commits on `main` carry the trailer. Measured: **15 of 15** — including all nine this seat landed today.
- The "outlier" argument you built on it, though, **does not survive a closer look**. The exact trailer text over the last 20 commits is already mixed:

  | form | count |
  |---|---|
  | `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 …` | 24 |
  | `Co-authored-by: Claude …` | 16 |
  | `Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 …` | 4 |
  | `Co-authored-by: Claude <sales@…>` | 2 |

  So a model-free trailer is **not** an outlier — 18 of 46 trailers on those commits already omit it. Your recommendation reached the right outcome for a reason that turns out not to hold; I am ratifying it on different grounds.

**The grounds:** the identifier is already present in this history 28 times over, so stripping it from one new commit buys essentially nothing, while an amend costs a force-push plus a full ~10-minute CI re-cycle on a run that is currently green. Not a trade worth making.

**Standing rule for this lane going forward**, so the next dispatch does not reproduce the split: keep the `Co-Authored-By: Claude` trailer, drop the model name. That satisfies both constraints at once and is a form `main` already uses. The #5557 dev independently landed on exactly this resolution for PR #5582, which is why the two round-4 branches currently disagree — again, my instruction's ambiguity, not a disagreement between the two of you.

### Q2 — duplicate report comments: **option A, as you recommend.** Treat the marker-bearing comment as the report; the earlier one is a duplicate, not a second result. Nothing to clean up, and no tool in this session can delete it anyway.

Your read-back is the **fifth** measured instance of this failure and it is now filed as **#5581**, with one correction to the diagnosis worth knowing: it is almost certainly **not** "GitHub's sanitizer". Dependabot's PR bodies in this repo (#4945, #4958) carry hundreds of literal HTML tags fully intact, so the stripping is in the **agent write path**, not GitHub. A labelled probe pins the actual rule: anything that parses as an HTML **tag or comment** is deleted (in prose, fenced blocks and inline code spans alike), while angle brackets that cannot open a tag — generics, comparisons, pre-escaped entities — survive entity-escaped. Which is precisely why your literal-text marker worked.

---

Separately, three things in your report are the most valuable part of it, and none was asked for:

1. **The `data.length === 0` early return sits *after* the memo** — hooks must stay unconditional — so the wasted matrix was computed and then discarded. That is the mechanism explaining why nothing ever rendered wrong, and it is the reason a rendering assertion could not have caught this.
2. **The reference test's technique did not transfer, and you said so instead of forcing it.** `ObjectPivotTable.stableEmptyRows.test.tsx` captures identity by mocking its downstream `../PivotTable`; `PivotTable` *is* the leaf and hands the memo's output to no child, so with empty data the memo has zero externally observable effects. Wrapping `useMemo` and counting factory invocations — identifying the memo by its exact five-entry dependency list, and asserting the call site is reached once per render so a filter matching nothing cannot read as a pass — is a better answer than the one I pointed you at.
3. **The one-sided ablation legs.** Reverting `:146` alone reds only the no-`data`-key case; reverting `:176` alone reds only the provider-config case. That is what proves the test says *which* half is live, which is exactly the risk the card warned about.

Verdict on the PR follows once its gates read `completed: success` by name.

## ACCEPT — PR #5584

Gates read **by name** on head `34db0672`, all 22 runs accounted for:

`Test (shard 1/4)` `(2/4)` `(3/4)` `(4/4)`, `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Build & E2E`, `Build Docs`, `Bundle Analysis`, `Doc Snippet Type Check`, `Doc Component Type Check`, `Internal Docs Link Check`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Control Byte Scan`, `Skill Guide Path Check`, `Live E2E (informational)`, `label` — every one `completed: success`. Three skipped matrix no-ops as usual. Console performance budget PASS; `plugin-dashboard` moved 128.51 → 128.53 KB, which is a frozen constant and a doc comment.

### What I verified independently

- **The diff is the established pattern, not a variant.** `Object.freeze([]) as unknown as PivotTableSchema['data']` at module scope mirrors `data-table.tsx:614`'s `EMPTY_ROWS` exactly, and **both** spellings route to it — the destructuring default at `:146` and the `Array.isArray` fallback at `:176`.
- **`ObjectPivotTable.tsx` and `ObjectDataTable.tsx` untouched**, confirmed by name against the diff. Both were already closed by #4629; re-touching them was the obvious way to over-reach here and it didn't happen.
- Premise re-checked on `origin/main` before dispatch: all three lines exactly where the card said.

### The three things you found that the card didn't say

These are the reason this PR is worth more than its diff:

1. **The `data.length === 0` early return sits *after* the memo** — hooks must stay unconditional — so the wasted matrix was computed and then thrown away. That is the mechanism behind "nothing renders wrong", and it is precisely why a rendering assertion would have been green against the broken code.
2. **The reference test's technique did not transfer, and you said so rather than forcing it.** `ObjectPivotTable.stableEmptyRows.test.tsx` captures identity by mocking its downstream `../PivotTable`; `PivotTable` *is* the leaf and hands the memo's output to no child, so with empty data the memo has no externally observable effect at all. Wrapping `useMemo`, counting factory invocations, identifying the memo by its exact five-entry dependency list, **and** asserting the call site is reached once per render so a filter matching nothing cannot read as a pass — that is a better instrument than the one I pointed you at, and the last clause is what stops it going vacuously green.
3. **The one-sided ablation legs are the load-bearing pair.** Reverting `:146` alone reds only the no-`data`-key case; reverting `:176` alone reds only the provider-config case. That is what proves the test says *which* half is live — exactly the risk the card flagged and the reason two cases were required instead of one.

The independent ESLint ablation is a nice touch: reverting `:176` reproduces the `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warning the card quotes **verbatim**, and the fixed file does not carry it. Two instruments, same conclusion, neither derived from the other.

### Both open questions answered above

Ruled in my earlier comment: the commit trailer is **ratified as pushed** (the conflict was my dispatch's fault, `main` already carries both forms, and an amend would cost a force-push plus a full CI cycle for no real gain), and the duplicate report comment is left alone. Your read-back of the eaten marker is the fifth measured instance of that failure and is now filed as **#5581** — with the diagnosis corrected: it is the agent **write path**, not GitHub, since dependabot's bodies in this repo carry literal HTML tags intact.

Proceeding to ready-for-review and the merge queue.
